bib.title: Failing Loudly: An Empirical Study of Methods for Detecting Dataset Shift

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Failing Loudly: An Empirical Study of Methods for Detecting Dataset Shift", Stephan Rabanser, Stephan Günnemann, Zachary C. Lipton. Printed on p1: "33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), Vancouver, Canada." and "arXiv:1810.11953v4 [stat.ML] 28 Oct 2019". The filename says 2018, but the printed venue year is 2019.

COVERAGE: 38 of 38 pages; 79,547 of 79,547 chars extracted and read.
- References (pp10-13) were skimmed for origins.
- Appendix pp14-38 is only plots: I read captions, panel labels and axis ticks. I did not read the plot curves, and the appendix has no prose results beyond its short intro.
- I rendered pp7-8 as images. p7 was needed for table colours and fonts.

CLAIMS (setup below applies unless a claim says otherwise)
Common setup, p5-6:
- Main data: MNIST (50k/10k/10k) and CIFAR-10 (40k/10k/10k). The shift is applied to the test set only.
- Significance level: α = 0.05. Results are averaged over 5 random splits.
- Test samples: s ∈ {10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 10000}. MMD stops at 1000.
- Reduction to K = 32 for PCA, SRP, UAE and TAE. BBSDs outputs C dimensions. BBSDh and Classif output 1.
- Label and domain classifiers: ResNet-18. Autoencoders: 3 conv layers + 1 fully connected.
- Tests: KS + Bonferroni per dimension, MMD (permutation p-value), chi-squared for BBSDh, binomial for Classif.
- Shifts: adversarial (FGSM), knock-out, Gaussian noise (σ 1/10/100), image, two combinations. δ ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1.0}.

- claim: The best overall method is univariate KS with Bonferroni on the softmax outputs of a pretrained label classifier (BBSDs). It leads at every sample size.

LIMITS
- Scope: mostly image classification. Results on text, graphs, tabular data or other domains are not shown; the authors name NLP and graphs as future work.
- Not online: streaming detection is left open because adjacent time steps are correlated. Repeated daily testing is therefore not covered, nor is correction for testing many windows over time.
- Dimensionality reduction can miss shifts by construction. The authors speculate this is unlikely outside adversarial settings: "trivial to construct pathological cases"; "not put forth as a defense against worst-case adversarial attacks" (p3).
- No false-positive rate is tabulated. The no-shift case is included (p6) and shown only as plots (e.g. Fig 3a, Figs 47-54 panel a).
- "Detection accuracy" is never defined. It reads as the share of runs where the test rejects (my reading). Most Table 1b values step in about 1/30, which fits 2 datasets × 3 δ × 5 splits (my inference, not stated).
- Pooled figures mix two datasets and all shift strengths, and only 5 splits per setting, so small gaps between methods are weak evidence. The authors report error bars in plots, not in tables.
- The KS p-value results use α = 0.05. No effect-size threshold is studied, and the paper does not address over-sensitivity at very large samples.
- The domain-classifier heuristics need the classifier to detect first: "No samples available as Classif did not detect a shift" for CIFAR-10 knock-out and small noise, and for Fashion MNIST and CIFAR-10 original splits (Figs 29, 35, 49, 51).
- Sample-removal attribution for non-domain detectors was tried and dropped: "the results we obtained were unremarkable" (p5).
- Malignancy results are qualitative verdicts. No accuracy of the verdict itself, label budget or threshold is reported.
- Dated: this is 2019 work using ResNet-18 and Keras, and the tool footnote may no longer hold.

CODE: no snippets in the PDF. The paper points to https://github.com/steverab/failing-loudly (p6; Python, sklearn, Keras). I did not inspect that repository.

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p2: "Our pipeline for detecting dataset shift." It shows source and target, then reduction, then two-sample tests, then a combined decision, which is the whole method at a glance.
- Fig 2, p8: "Shift detection results for medium image shift on MNIST." Panels pair p-value decay with sample size against true accuracy p/q and the Classif estimate, with exemplars. It shows detection and harm together.
- Fig 3, p8: "Shift detection results on COIL-100 dataset." It shows a detected shift with flat accuracy, the clearest benign-shift picture.
- Fig 4, p9: "Difference plot for training and test set sixes." It is a concrete hidden shift in a famous dataset.
- Table 1, p7, has no figure number but carries the main results.
- Figs 5-54, pp14-38, are per-shift appendix plots with univariate and multivariate pairs. They are for reference, not teaching.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions were found.
- pypdf drops table colour and bold, so the "best/worst" and harmless/harmful marks come from rendered p7 plus PyMuPDF span colours, not from quotable text. The verdict lists therefore have no verbatim quote. The worst-method marks are also colour-only.
- Quotes join line breaks with spaces, and table quotes join rows with " / ". Ligatures are kept as extracted. Subscripts are lost ("s gn" is s_gn). Equations are garbled, and the tick labels "101, 102" are 10^1, 10^2.
- The source contradicts itself in three places:
  1. p7 lists m_gn as both "easily detectable" and "hard to detect". Table 1b (0.37 at 10,000 for BBSDs) fits hard.
  2. The Table 1a caption says "both UAE and TAE perform best" for multivariate, while p6 and the table's marks name UAE alone. TAE ties UAE only at 200.
  3. "BBDSs" on p7 is a typo for BBSDs.
